subject: Helios Health: one-way egress silence after private cutover
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@helioshealth.com>
To: avery.johnson@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-17T08:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Cutover complete — remote services unreachable from on-prem

Hi Avery,

We finished the private cutover to Redwood Private last night and are seeing a weird symptom: our backend services in the datacenter can reach Redwood-hosted endpoints (health checks succeed), but outbound traffic from our application servers to external APIs intermittently experiences a one-way failure — packets leave the host but replies never arrive. The problem started roughly 01:30-02:00 UTC and has been intermittent since.

I've attached a short pcap from one affected server plus a tcpdump-based traceroute. You can see SYNs go out and the external host responds, but our server never gets the SYN-ACK (or gets it very late). Any hints? We're blocked on a few customer integrations.

Attachments: helios_pcap_09017.pcap, helios-trace-09-17.txt

Thanks,
Alice Nguyen
Lead SRE, Helios Health
ops@helioshealth.com

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@helioshealth.com>
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-17T08:29:00Z
Subject: Re: Cutover complete — remote services unreachable from on-prem

Hi Alice — thanks for the quick flag and for the attachments.

We're looking now. A few quick asks that will speed triage:
- Can you confirm if the affected servers are behind a NAT gateway or using SNAT on your edge firewall?
- Can you run `ss -tanp` around the failure window and share ephemeral port usage?
- If possible, a packet capture at your edge device (prior to any SNAT) would help check for asymmetric return paths.

Grace & Lauren: tagging you for immediate triage. My preliminary read is this could be: ephemeral port exhaustion on an SNAT pool OR MTU/fragmentation leading to silent drops during TCP handshake (the pcap shows partial replies).

I'll coordinate a remediation play depending on what we find.

—Avery
Avery Johnson
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: avery.johnson@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: alice.nguyen@helioshealth.com
Date: 2026-09-17T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Cutover complete — remote services unreachable from on-prem

Forwarding initial findings after a quick look at the pcap and trace your team sent:

- Observed repeated SYN packets from the Helios host to api.thirdparty.com (dst port 443). There are matching SYN-ACKs from the remote IP, but the timestamps show the SYN-ACKs arriving on a different ingress interface in the cloud transit and not being forwarded back to the same path (asymmetric return).
- On a handful of flows we see DF set on the client-side and an MSS reduction / ICMP fragmentation-needed message in the upstream path, but those ICMP messages are being rate-limited and not consistently reaching the Helios host.
- There are also signs of ephemeral port reuse on the NAT device — short-lived port recycling in <1s for high-connection-rate flows. That can lead to misattributed replies when the connection table is churned.

Actionable short list:
1) Can Helios temporarily expand SNAT port pool (or add a second SNAT IP) and monitor for drop in failures?
2) Apply MSS clamp on the on-prem firewall to 1350 for the affected subnet to avoid fragmentation.
3) Check Security Group / firewall state timeouts — increase TCP established timeout by 30s to avoid premature state expiry during bursts.

I'll draft a targeted remediation plan and a brief canary rollback.

-Grace
Grace O'Connor
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: alice.nguyen@helioshealth.com, avery.johnson@redwood.com
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-17T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Cutover complete — remote services unreachable from on-prem

Alice — following Grace's triage, proposed remediation runbook (low-risk canary first):

Canary window (target 15-30 minutes):
- Step 0: Notify ops (Helios) and Redwood on-call.
- Step 1: Add one extra SNAT IP to the Helios edge NAT pool (or expand ephemeral range by +20000 ports).
- Step 2: Enable MSS clamping at the firewall for the application subnet (1350).
- Step 3: Reduce connection churn for a small subset of callers (deploy rate-limit) or pin port allocation temporarily if app supports it.
- Step 4: Monitor pcap/traces and TCP metrics (retransmits, SYN-ACK latency) in the canary window.
- Rollback: Remove added SNAT IP and MSS clamp if failures increase; if successful, gradually apply to remaining subnets.

Estimated impact: brief connection restarts for canary hosts; no config changes to Redwood Private control plane.

Marissa — can you approve 4-hour maintenance window for Helios to run canary steps? I suggest a brief billing credit if we need to escalate to on-prem firewall vendor.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Technical Lead, Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@helioshealth.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, avery.johnson@redwood.com
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-18T14:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Cutover complete — remote services unreachable from on-prem

Team — quick update: we performed the canary this morning (added SNAT IP + applied MSS clamp 1350) per Lauren's steps across 20 app servers. Results: no more one-way failures observed during a 3-hour monitoring window. Retransmits dropped ~92%, SYN-ACK latencies normalized.

We reverted the canary (kept MSS clamp) while we decide whether to keep the SNAT IP expansion permanently. Ops validated there were no downstream side effects.

Next steps we've agreed:
- Temporary mitigation: keep MSS clamp for 72 hours and monitor.
- Permanent: expand ephemeral port allocation and schedule a controlled SNAT pool increase with final cutover next week.
- Redwood to prepare a one-page postmortem and recommended runbook additions (MSS clamp as standard after private cutovers; SNAT sizing guidance).

Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround — big help.

Alice
Lead SRE, Helios Health
